title: Suspicious script or LOLBin payload in a Run key
description: Detects a Run, RunOnce or Explorer policy Run value set to a selected script payload or suspicious signed Windows utility command.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may establish logon persistence by placing a script or proxy-execution command in a Windows Run registry value.
hypothesis.rationale: MITRE recommends monitoring Run-key changes that introduce unusual binary paths or script-based payloads. Restricting the rule to selected user-writable script locations and behavior-bearing PowerShell, Mshta, Regsvr32 or Rundll32 commands avoids the high volume produced by alerting on every Run-key value set.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify selected script and LOLBin payloads written to Run, RunOnce or Explorer policy Run keys while leaving ordinary application startup values, unrelated registry keys and non-set actions unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint registry events

triage.summary: Validate the new startup value, payload origin and writer before escalation; approved applications can use Run keys, but script and behavior-bearing LOLBin payloads require explanation.
steps: Review the complete registry key, value name and value data together with the initiating process, command line, account and endpoint role.
Inspect the referenced script or remote resource, verify its signer or hash where available and correlate file creation, download and subsequent logon execution.
Confirm an approved software deployment or logon workflow; otherwise remove the persistence safely, contain the endpoint and investigate the originating process and account.
false_positives: Approved logon scripts, software updaters or management tooling that intentionally place a selected script or LOLBin command in a Run key

validation.expected_outcome: Match selected user-writable script payloads or suspicious PowerShell, Mshta, Regsvr32 and Rundll32 commands written to Run keys; do not match ordinary startup values, unrelated keys or deletion events.
